sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.275/2023 was registered by R. T. Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru City for the aforesaid offences against the petitioner herein and two others based on the complaint dated 12.08.2023 lodged by Smt. Radha, who is the mother of deceased-Shilpa.
4.

sentences.text: During the course of investigation of the case, the petitioner was arrested on 21.08.2023 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.

Bail application filed by petitioner before the Court of XLV Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge,

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, he is before this Court.

Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition, submits that the material on record would go to show that the deceased who is the wife of petitioner had deserted the petitioner and she was residing separately, there is no material to invoke section 304B of IPC against the accused.
Further proceedings in the case as against accused Nos.2 and 3 has been stayed by this Court in Criminal Petition No.7912/2023.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the petition.
She submits that prior to Shilpa committing suicide she had forwarded Whatsapp messages to her relatives stating petitioner was the cause for her death.

She also submits that there is sufficient material to Kamala Kannan vs State By R.T. Nagar Ps on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193965543/
2 show that the deceased was being harassed for dowry by the accused.

entities.text: Kamala Kannan vs State By R.T. Nagar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, she prays to dismiss the petition.
7. The material on record would go to show that the marriage of the petitioner with the deceased-Shilpa was NC: 2024:KHC:6528 solemnized on 17.03.2023.

As per the complaint and the charge sheet allegations, after the marriage the petitioner and other accused persons were demanding additional dowry and they were harassing the deceased in furtherance of their demand for additional dowry.
The material on record would go to show that the relationship between the petitioner and his wife was strained and she had taken shelter in her parents' house.

The material also goes to show that few days prior to deceased committing suicide, she had approached J.C.
Nagara Police Station, Bengaluru and had lodged a complaint, based on which a NCR case was registered by the said Police.

In the said complaint, dated 03.08.2023 which was lodged before the J.C Nagara Police Station, there was no allegation of demand for dowry by the accused persons nor there was any allegation about the ill-treatment in furtherance of demand made for dowry.
8. Allegation is now made against the accused persons that there was a demand for payment of NC:
2024:KHC:6528 additional dowry and in furtherance of such demand, accused had ill-treated and tortured the deceased.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
It is not in dispute that the further proceedings in the present case as against accused Nos.2 and 3 has been stayed by the co-ordinate bench of this Court in Criminal Petition No.7912/2023.

Even otherwise in the complaint that was lodged on 03.08.2023 before the J.C.Nagara Police Station by the deceased, there are no such averments with regard to demand of additional dowry or harassment by the accused persons in furtherance of such demand.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail is required to be answered in the affirmative.

Accordingly the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

The petitioner/accused No.1 is directed to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.275/2023 registered by R.T.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru City for NC: 2024:KHC:6528 the offences punishable under Sections 304B, 498A, 504 and 323 of IPC, subject to the following conditions:
i.

The petitioner/accused No.1 shall execute personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with 2 sureties for the like-sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court;
ii.

The petitioner/accused No.1 shall appear regularly on all the dates of hearing before the Trial Court unless the Trial Court exempts his appearance for valid reasons;
iii. The petitioner/accused No.1 shall not directly or indirectly threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
